note: Both sets cover the same core facts (solar altitude 50°, window azimuth 0, the Height = Depth*tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth – window azimuth) algorithm and its D*1.2 simplification, 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, powder-coated finish, 25-degree structural bend). Each repeats several facts under two names, but Set B additionally misbinds the 25-degree bend to the 'louver longitudinal section' as if it were the component, and duplicates the 1:1 ratio claim twice. Set A's only real flaw is one truncated condition string ('along the louver longit') alongside a complete version of the same claim, so it is marginally cleaner and more faithful.
remarks: Both sets omit the fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths (to preserve adequate shading for the non-uniform tapered shape), and neither captures the bend's function of directing reflected light and reducing direct glare. Both also repeat the spacing formula and the 1:1 ratio under two attribute names. Set A's condition field for one bend claim is cut off mid-word ('along the louver longit'), likely a truncation artifact in the extraction.
